text:
mei: FYI I finished initial bring-up of Argus7b-lite (Mistral-ish arch) on dedicated and started int4 quant experiments. Seeing a consistent summarization quality regression vs our Llama baseline when using our proj-order optimized exporter. Short repro and notes below.

raj: Can you paste the failing sample and the eval command?

mei: repro command:
```
# run eval harness
./eval/run_eval.sh --model argus7b-lite-int4 --workload summarization --batch 8 --seed 42
```
failing sample (prompt truncated):
"""
User: Summarize the following conversation into 3 bullets...
...
Expected: concise bullets about billing confusion and next steps
Got: repeated, lower-coherence output, hallucinated next-step (wrong owner)
"""

emma: interesting. did you compare against a non-optimized export? (i.e., same fp16 weights)

mei: yes. fp16 export (no proj-order rewrite, no quant) matches Llama baseline. The regression crops up only when int4 quant + proj-order swap are applied.

harry: proj-order swap meaning we changed the layout of the attention projection weights (we interleaved q/k/v-> optimized order) during conversion for faster kernels, right?

mei: exactly. converter currently does: reshape -> transpose -> pack into [heads, head_dim] but for some models the original training used a different logical layout; our swap might be mixing head groups across k/v which would change cross-head correlations.

raj: could also be a tokenizer/vocab quirk compounding the issue. Argus has a couple of oddities: (1) soft-hyphen folding, (2) emoji cluster tokenization different from Llama. If kv-cache indices shift then attention addressing could be wrong in long context.

mei: I checked token-level diffs for the prompt. Tokenization aligned for the root prompt, but long context examples show off-by-one in a few places when the converter applies pad alignment. Example snippet of token ids around the divergence:
```
# baseline token ids:  1203 45  678 999  2
# int4 converted ids: 1203 45  678 1000 2  <- note 999->1000 shift at eos handling
```

emma: that could be two independent issues: a) proj-order weight shuffle altering attention math, b) pad/eos handling causing token index offsets during kv-cache assembly. Both would wreck generation quality but in different ways.

harry: quick sanity check: can you run the int4 model but disable proj-order reordering in the runtime (i.e., keep storage layout as-converted but have runtime read it q/k/v in original positions)? If the regression disappears it's weight-layout related.

mei: running now. command:
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_OVERRIDES=READ_PROJ_AS_ORIG=1
./serve_local.sh --model argus7b-lite-int4 --port 9102 --no-autobatch
```

ci-bot: deploy-check: port 9102 started, health ok, p95 latency 83ms (local toy), running eval suite (queued).

mei: preliminary: with READ_PROJ_AS_ORIG=1 the quality gap shrank significantly. Same prompts now match baseline summary style for >90% of test set. So root cause is almost certainly proj-order mismatch.

raj: nice find. So conversion step is the culprit. Two follow-ups: 1) add robust per-layer projection-layout fingerprinting during conversion to detect nonstandard q/k/v packing, 2) add small unit test in the eval harness to compare logits on a short prefix across wasm/fp16/int4 exports to detect silent math changes.

emma: for the immediate fix: add a converter flag to preserve source projection ordering (no re-packing) for models that fail fingerprints. Also add an adapter shim in the runtime to remap projections on load (fast, but avoids re-exporting).

harry: I'll sketch the shimming logic. Essentially: when header->proj_fingerprint != expected, load raw weights and apply per-head slice remap P such that P @ W_conv = W_orig. We already do similar for head-concat variants.

mei: low-priority note: we still see a tiny residual diff on long-context summarization even after fixing proj-order — likely due to that pad/eos token id shift Raj noted. I will open a separate triage to track tokenization edgecases (emoji clusters + soft-hyphen) vs kv-cache assembly.

raj: sounds good. Action items:
- mei: open two PRs: converter fingerprint + tokenization-kv-cache testcases (include the failing long-context samples)
- harry: prototype runtime shim + perf check (should be <2% p95 penalty)
- emma: add an eval guard that compares per-token next-token logits for first 64 tokens across exports and flags >1e-3 L2 diff

mei: I'll drop the failing examples into /eval/artifacts/argus7b-lite/ and link in the PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:

harry: ping me if you want pair on the remap matrix math.

ci-bot: ticket created: #INFR-4321 "Argus7b-lite proj-order conversion regression" assigned to mei/harry/raj, priority P2.
